title: Small-Practice Addition to Repayment Plan Runs — Network Participation Agreements
content:
A small practice repaying overpayments on one of its **Network Participation Agreements** through a repayment plan is given more claim payment runs. Whether a practice is small depends on its documented employee headcount.

## Documented headcount

The only headcount documentation Cascade holds for a practice is the census report on the practice's own Cascade staff group contract, held under **Employer Group Contracts**. The headcount is the number of eligible employees on the most recent census report of that contract, while the contract has not ended. A contract that has not ended is one in applied or active status.

## Addition to the plan run count

- A documented headcount of fewer than 5 employees adds 6 runs.
- A documented headcount of 5 up to 19 employees adds 3 runs.
- A practice with no such census on file, whose contract has ended, or with a larger documented headcount is on the standard terms and adds nothing.

## Decision table

| The practice's staff contract under Employer Group Contracts | Eligible employees on the latest census | Runs added |
|---|---|---|
| Applied or active, census on file | 1 to 4 | 6 |
| Applied or active, census on file | 5 to 19 | 3 |
| Applied or active, census on file | 20 or more | None |
| Applied or active, no census on file | — | None |
| Ended | — | None |
| No staff group contract | — | None |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A staff contract is in applied status, and its only census reports 19 eligible employees: 3 runs are added.
- An active staff contract whose census reported 4, then 22 on the latest report: the latest report governs, and nothing is added.
